newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Western world nickel output slides in July - INSG.
newsitem.headline: Western world nickel output slides in July - INSG.

text.p: Nickel mine production in the western world fell sharply in July, tumbling to 47,800 tonnes from 61,700 in June, data from the International Nickel Study Group (INSG) showed.
Primary nickel production in the western world was down to 50,900 tonnes in July from 58,200 in June.
The reason behind the fall was a plunge in key Canadian mine production in July to 5,300 tonnes from 17,000 a month earlier. Primary output there fell to 3,000 from 10,200.

The INSG said the drop in Canada was typical for a month when summer holiday closures and the renegotiation of work contracts slowed production. The mine and primary output figures for July 1995 were given as 4,400 and 3,600 tonnes respectively.

Elsewhere, figures were relatively stable. Indonesian mine output dropped 900 tonnes to 6,900 tonnes and Australian mine production was 500 tonnes lower at 8,900. Despite this, primary production in Australia climbed to 6,300 tonnes from 5,700.
On the consumption side, western world offtake dipped slightly to 71,300 tonnes in July from 73,500 in June.
European Union offtake remained generally weak at 27,400 tonnes against 29,100. German consumption fell 500 tonnes to 6,500 and the UK's was down 300 tonnes at 3,500.
